source.snippet: If I want to know what some iShares or Xtrackers fund is actually holding I can just download some predictably structured URL. Easy. Try the same thing with Amundi — need to manually click through pointless prompts. Then not even a download URL on the fund website, just a bunch of scripted mess that sometimes manages to correctly convert the displayed graph data.

problem_statement: Retail and semi-professional ETF investors in Europe struggle to programmatically access fund holdings data because many fund providers (especially non-iShares) hide it behind dynamic scripting, cookie walls, and inconsistent formats, making portfolio analysis and due diligence unnecessarily difficult.
target_segment: Self-directed retail investors and independent financial analysts in Europe who actively research ETF holdings for portfolio construction or compliance
notes: A unified ETF holdings aggregator/API for European funds (Amundi, DWS, Lyxor, etc.) could have B2C and B2B angles. SFDR/MiFID compliance adds further demand.
